hypothesis: The combined runtime can preserve the canonical typesafe_sister package and its client while satisfying the historical wrapper's typesafe_sister.app attribute by exposing the existing typesafe_legacy.app before importing the wrapper.

baseline.command: fresh-process import of jev_gateway in a TemporaryDirectory reproducing the exact Docker COPY layout with a synthetic wrapper matching the observed typesafe_sister.app consumer

scope.allowed_change: A gateway-local compatibility binding established before letta_bridge_v2 import, without replacing the canonical package or changing launcher digest checks, routing, authentication, or provider selection.
forbidden_change: edit or push the auto-deployed source branch
sys.modules alias that replaces or hides the typesafe_sister package
edit the canonical typesafe_sister package without a separately proven need
change wrapper digest verification, secrets, authentication, provider routing, or catch-all ownership
merge, deploy, restart, production probe, paid preview, or new runtime resource

falsifiers: The exact Docker COPY layout still fails to import in a fresh process.
The synthetic observed wrapper receives an app other than typesafe_legacy.app.
typesafe_sister.client becomes unimportable or resolves through an alias.
A /jev route remains behind the legacy catch-all.
Missing or wrong bearer tokens reach any provider call.
A valid authenticated mocked request no longer returns the existing contract.
Any test performs provider or network egress.

promotion_gate.authorized_publication: distinct candidate branch and bounded draft PR only

known_limits: The real environment-materialized wrapper bytes are unavailable in this session; the wrapper fixture is synthetic and tests only the observed consumer contract.
Local import and HTTP tests cannot prove Railway startup, healthcheck success, provider reachability, or production recovery.
The candidate is based on the Railway source ref rather than main because the combined runtime files do not exist on main.
